scope: Current core/db.py, notify.py, collector.py, official_trace.py, dedup.py; offline synthetic fixtures only.
decision: Two reproducible P2 issues remain. This is not full-system acceptance or a production/deployment authorization.

findings.problem: Read-only user_version inspection is outside the migration writer reservation. An independent writer can publish a future version after inspection, and this initializer then runs old DDL and resets user_version to 1.
findings.reproduction: Seed normal Database. Subclass connect() solely to schedule a second real SQLite connection committing PRAGMA user_version=2 after inspection and before migration connection. RacingDatabase construction succeeds; observed version_after=1, rejected=false.
findings.impact: A concurrent future-version upgrade loses its compatibility marker; old code can continue against unknown schema. This is a deterministic legal connection interleaving, not a stress test or a claim that a future production version currently exists.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep the early read-only check, but recheck user_version under BEGIN IMMEDIATE before any DDL and fail/rollback if unsupported. Preserve that same reservation through all migration statements; a second executescript() implicitly commits, so do not accidentally release the lock while splitting the script.

findings.problem: reindex arbitrates only SENT/CLAIMED loser notices. INSERT OR IGNORE then discards a colliding RETRY or UNCERTAIN loser, including its later cooldown and attempt count.
findings.reproduction: Two synthetic historical key variants reindex into one event. Survivor telegram notice RETRY at now+300; loser same channel/batch RETRY (or UNCERTAIN), attempts=2, next_attempt=now+7200. After reindex: only survivor RETRY remains, next_attempt=now+300, attempts=0. SENT and CLAIMED variants pass.
findings.impact: A valid server 429 cooldown can be shortened by campaign migration even though the current sender correctly records it. Ambiguous delivery metadata may likewise disappear.
findings.minimal_fix: For conflicting nonterminal, non-active-claim notices, preserve max(next_attempt) and max(attempts), with UNCERTAIN precedence when either side is uncertain. Keep SENT terminal and preserve existing active CLAIMED fencing; explicitly test RETRY/RETRY and RETRY/UNCERTAIN alongside SENT/CLAIMED controls.
